questions.question: Vectorization loop se kyun tez hai?
questions.answer: Loop Python interpreter me per-element kaam karta hai (object boxing + type checks), jabki vectorized ops C loops me chalti hain aur SIMD use karti hain. Isliye rule: loop likhne se pehle vectorized alternative dhundo.
questions.explanation: C loop vs Python loop.

questions.question: Boolean mask indexing kaise kaam karta hai?
questions.answer: arr[arr > 5] ek boolean array se filter karta hai aur copy return karta hai. Combine ke liye & | ke saath parentheses lagana zaroori hai, kyunki comparison operators ki precedence zyada hoti hai.
questions.explanation: Mask banao, phir index karo.

questions.question: reshape aur resize me farq batao.
questions.answer: reshape view/na utna memory share karke naya shape deta hai (elements total same hone chahiye), resize original array ko in-place badalta hai (size badha bhi sakta hai). Data safe rakho to reshape.
questions.explanation: Reshape safe, resize in-place.

questions.question: hstack/vstack aur concatenate me choice kaise karte hain?
questions.answer: Rows jodne ke liye concatenate([a, b], axis=0) ya vstack, columns ke liye axis=1 ya hstack. Explicit axis wala concatenate sabse clear hai aur dimension mismatch par saaf error deta hai.
questions.explanation: Axis explicit likho.

questions.question: Random seed set karna testing me kyun zaroori hai?
questions.answer: Reproducibility ke liye: default_rng(42) se same data har run me milta hai, isliye tests stable rehte hain. Production me alag seeds use karo par test fixtures me fixed.
questions.explanation: Fixed seed = stable tests.

questions.question: NumPy me NaN handle karne ke kaunse tools hain?
questions.answer: np.isnan se detect, np.nanmean/np.nansum se skip karke aggregate, np.nan_to_num se replace. Dhyan: NaN ke saath koi bhi comparison False hota hai, isliye == nahi, isnan use karo.
questions.explanation: NaN skip karke aggregate karo.

questions.question: Vectorized ops me float precision ka dhyan kyun rakhna chahiye?
questions.answer: Float64 me bhi 0.1 exact nahi hota, isliye == comparison fail karta hai. Fixed-point/cents me paisa rakho, aur comparison ke liye np.isclose(rtol=..., atol=...) use karo.
questions.explanation: Float equality kabhi reliable nahi.

questions.question: dtype casting ke rules kya hain (int + float, int8 overflow)?
questions.answer: Mixed ops me safe/common type choose hota hai (int64 + float64 → float64). Fixed-width int overflow wrap kar jaata hai (int8 127+1 = -128), isliye large numbers ke liye int64/float use karo.
questions.explanation: Promotion up, overflow chupke se.

questions.question: In-place operators (+=, *=) ka fayda aur khatra kya hai?
questions.answer: Memory bachate hain (naya array nahi banta) aur cache-friendly hote hain; khatra ye hai ki dtype mismatch par error aata hai aur view/shared buffer use ho sakta hai — 'a += 1' ne aisa bug banaya jo 'a = a + 1' me nahi tha.
questions.explanation: Memory bachta hai, dtype sharp rehta hai.

questions.question: Aggregate ke saath nan handling kaise karte hain (mean example)?
questions.answer: np.nanmean(x) NaN skip karke mean deta hai (np.mean nan deta hai). Ya pehle mask se NaN hatao: x[~np.isnan(x)]. Which is right depends: silently skip karna metric ko optimistic bana sakta hai — count bhi report karo.
questions.explanation: Skip karo par count bhi dikhao.

questions.question: Memory layout (C order vs F order) aur performance ka rishta kya hai?
questions.answer: C order row-major hai, isliye row direction me iterate karna cache-friendly hota hai (F order column-major). Bade arrays me layout mismatch random access dega aur speed chali jaayegi — np.ascontiguousarray se fix karo.
questions.explanation: Access pattern layout se match karao.

questions.question: dot/matmul aur elementwise * me farq batao.
questions.answer: * elementwise multiply karta hai (shape mismatch par broadcast/error), @ ya np.matmul matrix product karta hai ((m,k)@(k,n) → (m,n)). Machine learning code me yahi sabse common confusion hai.
questions.explanation: * elementwise, @ linear algebra.

questions.question: Bade arrays me memory blow-up se kaise bachte ho?
questions.answer: Views/slices use karo, in-place ops, float32 instead of float64, chunk/batch processing, aur output ko preallocate karo. Kabhi-kabhi ek expression (a - b) ** 2 do temporary arrays banata hai — isliye steps me likho aur del karo.
questions.explanation: Dtype + in-place + chunks.

questions.question: np.where ka use-case batao.
questions.answer: Conditional selection: np.where(cond, a, b) vectorized if-else hai — jaise negative values ko 0 karna, ya grade assign karna. Nested conditions ke liye np.select zyada readable hai.
questions.explanation: Vectorized if-else.

questions.question: (3,1) aur (1,4) arrays ka sum ka shape kya hoga?
questions.answer: (3, 4) — dono size-1 dimensions stretch hote hain (broadcast). Agar dono axes me size >1 aur unequal hoti to ValueError aata.
questions.explanation: Size-1 stretch hoti hai.

questions.question: print(np.array([1, 2, 3]) / 2) aur print(np.array([1, 2, 3]) // 2) ke output batao.
questions.answer: Pehla [0.5, 1, 1.5] (true division float deta hai), doosra [0, 1, 1] (floor division). Integer array me // silently truncate karta hai — percentage nikalte waqt yahi bug aata hai.
questions.explanation: / float, // floor.

questions.question: x = np.arange(5); y = x[:3]; y[0] = 99; print(x[0]) — output?
questions.answer: 99 — slicing view deti hai, isliye y me change original x me dikhta hai. Independent copy ke liye y = x[:3].copy().
questions.explanation: Slice = shared buffer.

questions.question: np.array([True, True, False]).sum() kya deta hai?
questions.answer: 2 — booleans ko 0/1 maan kar sum hota hai (bina explicit cast ke). Isliye 'kitne pass hue' jaisa count mask.sum() se ek line me nikalta hai.
questions.explanation: Bool sum = count of True.

questions.question: x = np.array([1, 2, 3], dtype=np.int8); x[0] += 200; print(x[0]) — output?
questions.answer: Overflow wrap hota hai: 201 mod 256 = -55 (int8 range −128..127). Isliye currency/counters ke liye int64 ya float, aur range check input par karo.
questions.explanation: Fixed-width int silently wrap.

questions.question: print(np.nan == np.nan) — output aur uska practical asar?
questions.answer: False — NaN kisi ke bhi barabar nahi hota (khud ke bhi nahi). Isliye NaN ko dedupe/filter karne ke liye == use na karo; isnan() ya pandas ke special handling use karo.
questions.explanation: NaN ka comparison hamesha False.

questions.question: A shape (5,3) hai aur B shape (5,) — A * B ka output shape kya hoga?
questions.answer: (5, 3) — B right-align hokar (1,5) ban jaata hai, phir broadcasting (5,3) vs (5,) FAIL karta hai... sahi jawab: ye ValueError deta hai, kyunki trailing dims 3 vs 5 mismatch hain. Sahi intent ke liye B[:, None] se (5,1) banao.
questions.explanation: Trailing dims align hote hain — yahan mismatch.

questions.question: np.arange(6).reshape(2, 3) aur .reshape(3, 2) me element order kaise badalta hai?
questions.answer: Default C order me flatten hota hai (row-major), isliye reshape se same 1D sequence dobara groupped hoti hai — values wahi rehti hain, sirf arrangement badalta hai. Column-wise chahiye to order='F' do.
questions.explanation: Reshape data nahi badalta, arrangement badalta hai.

questions.question: x = np.array([0.1, 0.2, 0.3]); print(x.sum() == 0.6) — kya aayega?
questions.answer: False aayega (0.6000000000000001 jaisa value). Float precision ki wajah se equality fail hoti hai; np.isclose(x.sum(), 0.6) use karo.
questions.explanation: Float sums equality-safe nahi.

questions.question: arr[i] loop se vs arr.sum() — kis case me loop faster ho sakta hai?
questions.answer: Jab aapko har element par complex Python-level logic chalani ho (custom branching, dict lookups) — wahan Python loop hi hota hai. Pure arithmetic ke liye vectorized path almost always faster.
questions.explanation: Vectorized arithmetic par loop nahi jeetega.

questions.question: np.zeros((3,)) me 0.0 hai ya 0?
questions.answer: float64 ka 0.0 hai (zeros default float). Integer chahiye to dtype=int do — warna downstream me float dtype propagate hoti hai.
questions.explanation: Default dtype float64 hai.

questions.question: empty = np.empty(3); print(empty) — reliable hai?
questions.answer: Nahi — np.empty memory allocate karta hai par initialize nahi, isliye values garbage ho sakti hain (kabhi 0 dikh bhi sakta hai). Production me hamesha zeros/ones/full use karo.
questions.explanation: empty ka content undefined hai.

questions.question: 2D array ka mean(axis=0) aur mean() (bina axis) me kya farq hoga?
questions.answer: axis=0 per-column mean (length = columns) deta hai; bina axis poore array ka ek scalar mean deta hai. Aggregation ka output shape axis se hi decide hota hai.
questions.explanation: Axis do to shape bachta hai, warna scalar.

questions.question: print((np.array([1, 2]) + np.array([3, 4])).dtype) — int64 me?
questions.answer: int64 — same dtype wale ints ka result bhi int64 rehta hai. Float ke saath mixed karne par hi float me promote hota hai (int64 + float32 → float64).
questions.explanation: Promotion rules yaad rakho.

questions.question: arr = np.arange(6); view = arr.reshape(2, 3); view[0, 0] = 100; print(arr[0]) — output?
questions.answer: 100 — reshape ne view diya (data share), isliye mutation original me dikhta hai. Agar reshape possible nahi hota (non-contiguous), NumPy copy bana deta hai — isliye behaviour data par depend karta hai.
questions.explanation: Reshape view de sakta hai, copy bhi.

questions.question: arr.mean() ki jagah arr.sum() / arr.size likhne me kya risk hai?
questions.answer: NaN hone par mean() NaN deta hai (clear signal), par manual sum/size bhi NaN dega — asli risk: dtype. Integer array par sum() int overflow/size se galti deta hai aur size 0 par ZeroDivisionError. np.mean use karo.
questions.explanation: Builtin aggregate edge cases handle karta hai.

questions.question: Two arrays ka np.hstack([a, b]) 1D par kya karta hai?
questions.answer: Same as concatenate(axis=0) — 1D me horizontal/vertical ka farq nahi banta, isliye dono ek hi lamba vector dete hain. 2D me hstack columns jodta hai aur vstack rows.
questions.explanation: 1D me hstack == concatenate.

questions.question: np.random.default_rng(0).integers(0, 10, 3) ko dobara same seed se chalaya — same output?
questions.answer: Haan — Generator per-object state rakhta hai, isliye same seed se same sequence milti hai (reproducible). Legacy np.random.seed global state hai, isliye threaded tests me flaky ho sakta hai.
questions.explanation: Generator instance seeded = reproducible.

questions.question: ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (3,4) (3,) — fix kaise karoge?
questions.answer: Trailing dims mismatch hain (4 vs 3). Intent ke hisaab se b[:, None] se (3,1) banao ya axis specify karo — silently reshape karne se pehle data ka meaning verify karo.
questions.explanation: Broadcast error = shape contract ka error.

questions.question: Array ka mean NaN aa raha hai jabki data saaf dikhta hai. Pehla suspect?
questions.answer: Data me NaN ya inf hai (ya string se convert hote waqt fail hua). Fix: np.isnan(x).sum() se gino, phir np.nanmean ya imputation choose karo — silently skip karna metric badal deta hai.
questions.explanation: NaN count karo pehle.

questions.question: arr[mask] me change karne par original array update nahi hua. Wajah?
questions.answer: Boolean/fancy indexing copy deta hai, isliye assignment original par asar nahi karta. Fix: original par mask assign karo (arr[mask] = value) ya arr[bool_mask] ke bajaye np.where use karo.
questions.explanation: Mask copy banata hai, view nahi.

questions.question: Percentage nikalte waqt sab values 0 aa rahi hain (counts integer hain). Fix?
questions.answer: Integer division ne truncate kar diya. Fix: numerator ko float me convert karo (100.0 * a / b) ya dtype=float array banao.
questions.explanation: 100.0 likho, 100 nahi.

questions.question: in-place '+=' float value ke saath int array par TypeError de raha hai. Fix?
questions.answer: In-place op dtype nahi badal sakta, isliye int array me 0.5 add nahi hoga. Fix: pehle x = x.astype(float) karo, ya out-of-place x = x + 0.5 likho.
questions.explanation: In-place dtype change nahi karta.

questions.question: Array update kiya par dusra array bhi badal gaya (unexpected). Root cause?
questions.answer: Dono naam ek hi buffer share kar rahe the (slicing/view ya shallow copy). Fix: boundary par .copy() explicit likho, aur mutation se pehle np.shares_memory(a, b) se check karo.
questions.explanation: Shared buffer = shared mutation.

questions.question: axis=0 aur axis=1 ulta lag gaya, probabilities ka sum 1 nahi aa raha. Fastest fix?
questions.answer: Shape assertion add karo: assert out.shape == (rows,), taaki axis ka mistake crash kare. Axis confusion ka permanent ilaaj explicit shape checks aur named shapes/constants hain.
questions.explanation: Shape assert se axis bug pakdo.

questions.question: np.array(data) ka dtype object aa gaya (float ops fail). Wajah?
questions.answer: Data me mixed types (strings + numbers, ya None) hain, isliye NumPy object dtype chun leta hai. Fix: input saaf karo (float(v) with error handling) aur explicit dtype=float64 pass karo.
questions.explanation: Object dtype = mixed input.

questions.question: DecisionThreshold: comparisons '==' se float columns par rarely match kar rahe hain. Fix?
questions.answer: Float equality unreliable hai — np.isclose(rtol=1e-9) ya rounding (np.round(x, 6)) use karo; ya paisa/percent ko integer units me store karo.
questions.explanation: Equality ke liye isclose.

questions.question: Training loop memory badhta ja raha hai, kuch tensors free nahi ho rahe. Kya karoge?
questions.answer: References hold karne wale structures (list me store, closure capture) check karo, del + gc.collect() se verify karo, aur in-place ops/preallocation use karo. tracemalloc se growth ka exact site nikalo.
questions.explanation: Reference graph dekho, tracemalloc se confirm karo.

questions.question: numpy random results run-to-run badal rahe hain (test flaky). Fix?
questions.answer: Global np.random ke bajaye explicit Generator with fixed seed use karo aur use function me pass karo (inject karo). Isse test deterministic aur production path independent rehta hai.
questions.explanation: Seed inject karo, global state nahi.

questions.question: Sorting ke baad original array ka order badal gaya (jo nahi chahiye tha). Fix?
questions.answer: np.sort naya array deta hai (original safe), par a.sort() in-place hai. Galti se in-place call hua to copy = a.copy() pehle, ya np.sort use karo.
questions.explanation: sort() in-place, np.sort copy.

questions.question: Concatenate ke baad shape expected se alag aa gaya. Fastest diagnostic?
questions.answer: Har input ka .shape print karo aur expected (n, d) se compare karo — 90% cases me ek input 1D hai jise reshape/expand_dims chahiye. np.expand_dims(arr, 0) se fix hota hai.
questions.explanation: Shapes print karo, andaza nahi.

questions.question: Numeric drift: do tarike se sum kiya, results thode alag. Ye bug hai ya expected?
questions.answer: Expected hai — float addition order-se-sensitive hai (large + small me precision loss). Stable chahiye to Kahan summation ya pairwise/float128 use karo, aur tests me tolerance rakho (np.allclose).
questions.explanation: Order-dependent float math.

questions.question: Mask se delete kiya: x = np.delete(x, mask) — galat elements gaye. Wajah?
questions.answer: np.delete indices (ya boolean mask of same shape) expect karta hai, values nahi; boolean mask dene par woh positions delete karta hai. Sahi: x = x[~mask].
questions.explanation: Delete positions leta hai, conditions nahi.

questions.question: Bade array par stack banate waqt MemoryError aa gaya, par data chhota dikhta hai. Wajah?
questions.answer: Intermediate copies (broadcast results, dtype promotion to float64, list-vs-array conversion) memory multiply kar deti hain. Fix: dtype explicit rakho, in-place ops use karo aur chunk-wise process karo.
questions.explanation: Intermediates memory kha jaate hain.

questions.question: Performance: 1e7 elements par Python loop 30s le raha hai. Refactor kaise karoge?
questions.answer: Step 1: loop ko vectorized equivalent me likho (mask + np.where / arithmetic). Step 2: dtype float32/float64 check karo. Step 3: chunks me process karo agar memory tight hai. Measure karke bolo: loop 30s → vectorized 0.4s.
questions.explanation: Vectorize → dtype → chunk.

questions.question: np.set_printoptions(threshold=...) ke bina bade array ka print output hi nahi dikh raha. Quick fix?
questions.answer: Threshold badhao (np.set_printoptions(threshold=1000, linewidth=120)) ya slice print karo (arr[:10]) — production me logging ke liye counts/stats print karo, poora array nahi.
questions.explanation: Slice ya summary print karo.

questions.question: Division ne RuntimeWarning: invalid value encountered in divide diya. Isko kaise handle karoge?
questions.answer: Warning ignore mat karo: np.errstate ke saath to out=np.zeros_like(a), where=b != 0 use karo, ya NaN ko explicitly detect karke report karo — silently suppress karna data quality ka signal chhupa deta hai.
questions.explanation: where= se intent clear karo.

questions.question: Kaggle-style code me np.where ka output shape expected se alag hai. Wajah?
questions.answer: np.where(cond, a, b) me a/b broadcast hote hain — agar a scalar aur b column vector hai to result ka shape b se aata hai. Shapes explicitly likho aur result shape assert karo.
questions.explanation: Where broadcasting karta hai.

questions.question: np.where aur boolean mask me kab kaunsa choose karte ho?
questions.answer: Mask tab jab sirf filter/summary chahiye (arr[arr > 0], mask.sum()). np.where tab jab do values me se choose karna ho (replace, clip, conditional column) — read-only selection me mask sasta aur clearer hai.
questions.explanation: Select vs replace.

questions.question: Array se top-k largest values nikalo bina poori sorting ke.
questions.answer:
import numpy as np

def top_k(x, k=3):
    x = np.asarray(x)
    if k >= len(x):
        return np.sort(x)[::-1]
    part = np.partition(x, -k)[-k:]
    return np.sort(part)[::-1]
questions.explanation: partition O(n) hai, full sort O(n log n).

questions.question: np.array([1,2,3])[None, :].shape aur [:, None].shape — dono output batao.
questions.answer: (1, 3) aur (3, 1) — None se naya axis add hota hai (expand_dims ka shortcut), jo broadcasting ke liye row/column vector banata hai.

questions.question: np.arange(4).reshape(2,2).sum(axis=0, keepdims=True).shape — output?

questions.question: Explain: ndarray ko basic level par explain karo aur ek AI/data use case batao.
questions.answer: ndarray: NumPy ka homogeneous n-dimensional array. Example: np.array([1,2,3]). Pitfall: mixed dtypes or object arrays.
questions.explanation: USE / IMPACT: fast vectorized numeric workloads me.

questions.question: Define: dtype ko basic level par explain karo aur ek AI/data use case batao.
questions.answer: dtype: array element type specification. Example: dtype=np.float32. Pitfall: precision/range trade-off.

questions.question: Shape `(3, 2)` wale array me shape `(2,)` ka vector add karo, phir `(3, 1)` aur `(4,)` wala case sochо — kaun chalta hai aur result shape kya hoga?
questions.answer: `(3,2) + (2,)` → `(3,2)` aur `(3,2) + (3,1)` → `(3,2)` — trailing dimensions align hote hain (compatible jab equal ho ya ek 1 ho). `(3,2) + (4,)` → `ValueError`, kyunki 2 aur 4 na barabar hain na koi 1. `(3,1,4) + (4,)` → `(3,1,4)`.

questions.question: `a = np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4]])` par `a.mean(axis=0)` aur `a.mean(axis=1)` ka result likho.
questions.answer: `axis=0` → `[2.0, 3.0]` (column-wise: rows collapse hoti hain) aur `axis=1` → `[1.5, 3.5]` (row-wise: columns collapse hoti hain). Shape bhi badalta hai — `(2,2)` se `(2,)` dono case me, par kis axis ka index bacha wo alag hai.

questions.question: Normalization ke baad array me NaN aa rahe hain — sabse likely kya hai?
questions.answer: Do common wajah: (1) kisi column ka mean 0 hai ya std 0 hai → zero-division se NaN/inf, aur (2) input me pehle se NaN hai jo propagate ho gaya. Check karo `np.isnan(x).sum()` aur per-column std; fix `np.nanmean` + std-zero guard se.

questions.question: Kaun sa edge case row-wise normalization ganit ko todta hai?
questions.answer: Constant column (std = 0) → 0 se division. Guard: `if std == 0: std = 1` (ya us column ko normalize na karo), warna poora column NaN ban jata hai aur model usse kuch seekh nahi paata.

questions.question: Shape aur dtype validation kahan karo — data load karte waqt ya function ke andar?
questions.answer: Load boundary par strong validation (expected shape, 2D hona, dtype float, NaN count) aur function ke andar sirf sasta assert (`arr.ndim == 2`). Warna har numpy call par shape check kernal ki speed kha jata hai.

questions.question: Memory-bound pipeline me pehle kya optimize karoge: dtype, copies, ya vectorization?
questions.answer: Pehle unnecessary copies hatao (views chuno, `inplace`/out-parameter use karo), phir dtype downcast (`float64` → `float32` = half memory, aksar same accuracy), phir algorithm/vectorization. Har step ko memory-profiler se measure karo, andaaze se nahi.
